title: Regime-Dependent Validity in Energy-Flow Cosmology: Evidence from SPARC Galaxy Rotation Curves and the EFC-R Framework
description: A pilot-scale analysis of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) applied to 20 SPARC galaxies, demonstrating regime-dependent validity where EFC achieves 100% success for LSB and diffuse dwarf galaxies but systematically underperforms for structurally complex systems like barred spirals. Introduces the EFC-R framework with the decomposition E_total = E_flow + E_latent as a domain-of-validity layer for EFC.

energy_flow_field.description: Effective energy field governing circular velocities, where ρ is local energy density and S ∈ [0,1] is a normalized entropy field

circular_velocity.description: Circular velocity prediction from the energy-flow potential Φ_e

delta_aic.description: Model comparison metric; ΔAIC < −2 means EFC significantly preferred, > +2 means ΛCDM preferred

energy_decomposition.description: EFC-R regime decomposition separating flow-dominated energy from latent structural energy in complex systems

key_results.main_finding: EFC achieves 100% success rate for LSB and diffuse dwarf galaxies but 0% for barred/disturbed spirals, with structural complexity (latent field proxy) correlating with EFC performance at Spearman ρ = 0.705, p = 0.0005.

sealed_predictions.statement: EFC will achieve ≥90% success rate (ΔAIC ≤ 2 vs ΛCDM) for LSB galaxies in a larger independent SPARC sample (N ≥ 50 LSB galaxies)
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Applying EFC fitting to ≥50 LSB galaxies from SPARC and finding success rate < 90%

sealed_predictions.statement: The correlation between the latent field proxy L and EFC residuals will remain statistically significant (p < 0.01) in the full SPARC sample (N ≈ 175)
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Full SPARC analysis showing Spearman p ≥ 0.01 for L vs EFC performance

sealed_predictions.statement: EFC will systematically fail for barred spirals and morphologically disturbed galaxies, with ΔAIC > +2 for ≥80% of such systems
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Finding that EFC succeeds (ΔAIC ≤ 2) for >20% of barred/disturbed galaxies in a larger sample

kill_criteria: KC1: EFC fails to achieve ΔAIC ≤ 2 for ≥70% of LSB galaxies in an independent sample of N ≥ 50 LSB galaxies from SPARC, contradicting the claimed regime-dependent success
KC2: The Spearman correlation between structural complexity (latent field proxy L) and EFC performance drops below ρ = 0.3 or becomes statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) in the full SPARC sample
KC3: EFC mean χ²_red exceeds ΛCDM mean χ²_red across all morphological categories in a full SPARC analysis, eliminating any regime advantage
KC4: The entropy gradient parameter ∇S is unconstrained or varies by more than two orders of magnitude within a single morphological class, indicating the parameter is non-physical
KC5: Independent analysis shows that the latent field proxy L has no predictive power for distinguishing EFC-success vs EFC-failure galaxies in a blinded test
name: EFC-R-SPARC
